From e2febe375e5ea5afed92f4cd9711bde8f24ee6d2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Waqar Hameed <waqar.hameed@axis.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Dec 2025 23:36:02 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] power: supply: rt9455: Fix use-after-free in
 power_supply_changed()

Using the `devm_` variant for requesting IRQ _before_ the `devm_`
variant for allocating/registering the `power_supply` handle, means that
the `power_supply` handle will be deallocated/unregistered _before_ the
interrupt handler (since `devm_` naturally deallocates in reverse
allocation order). This means that during removal, there is a race
condition where an interrupt can fire just _after_ the `power_supply`
handle has been freed, *but* just _before_ the corresponding
unregistration of the IRQ handler has run.

This will lead to the IRQ handler calling `power_supply_changed()` with
a freed `power_supply` handle. Which usually crashes the system or
otherwise silently corrupts the memory...

Note that there is a similar situation which can also happen during
`probe()`; the possibility of an interrupt firing _before_ registering
the `power_supply` handle. This would then lead to the nasty situation
of using the `power_supply` handle *uninitialized* in
`power_supply_changed()`.

Fix this racy use-after-free by making sure the IRQ is requested _after_
the registration of the `power_supply` handle.

Fixes: e86d69dd786e ("power_supply: Add support for Richtek RT9455 battery charger")
Signed-off-by: Waqar Hameed <waqar.hameed@axis.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/1567d831e04c3e2fcb9e18dd36b7bcba4634581a.1766268280.git.waqar.hameed@axis.com
Signed-off-by: Sebastian Reichel <sebastian.reichel@collabora.com>

diff --git a/drivers/power/supply/rt9455_charger.c b/drivers/power/supply/rt9455_charger.c
index 1ffe7f02932f..5130d2395e88 100644
--- a/drivers/power/supply/rt9455_charger.c
+++ b/drivers/power/supply/rt9455_charger.c
@@ -1663,6 +1663,15 @@ static int rt9455_probe(struct i2c_client *client)
 	rt9455_charger_config.supplied_to	= rt9455_charger_supplied_to;
 	rt9455_charger_config.num_supplicants	=
 					ARRAY_SIZE(rt9455_charger_supplied_to);
+
+	info->charger = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &rt9455_charger_desc,
+						   &rt9455_charger_config);
+	if (IS_ERR(info->charger)) {
+		dev_err(dev, "Failed to register charger\n");
+		ret = PTR_ERR(info->charger);
+		goto put_usb_notifier;
+	}
+
 	ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, client->irq, NULL,
 					rt9455_irq_handler_thread,
 					IRQF_TRIGGER_LOW | IRQF_ONESHOT,
@@ -1678,14 +1687,6 @@ static int rt9455_probe(struct i2c_client *client)
 		goto put_usb_notifier;
 	}
 
-	info->charger = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &rt9455_charger_desc,
-						   &rt9455_charger_config);
-	if (IS_ERR(info->charger)) {
-		dev_err(dev, "Failed to register charger\n");
-		ret = PTR_ERR(info->charger);
-		goto put_usb_notifier;
-	}
-
 	return 0;
 
 put_usb_notifier:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

The patch fixes a use-after-free bug in the RT9455 battery charger driver (`drivers/power/supply/rt9455_charger.c`). The fix reorders two calls in the `rt9455_probe()` function:

1. **Move `devm_power_supply_register()` before `devm_request_threaded_irq()`**  
   In the original code, the threaded IRQ was registered *before* the power supply device was registered. With `devm_` managed resources, resources are freed in reverse order of allocation. This created a race condition during device removal:
   - The power supply handle could be freed *before* the IRQ handler was unregistered.
   - If an IRQ fired after the power supply was freed but before the IRQ handler was removed, `power_supply_changed()` would access freed memory, causing use-after-free.
   - Similarly, during probe, an IRQ could fire before the power supply was registered, leading to use of an uninitialized handle.

2. **Reorder to register power supply first**  
   By registering the power supply *before* requesting the IRQ, the reverse order of freeing ensures the IRQ handler is removed first, keeping the power supply handle valid during the entire lifetime of the interrupt. This eliminates both the use-after-free and the uninitialized access race conditions.

**Relationship between modifications**  
Both modifications occur in the same function (`rt9455_probe`) in a single file. The change moves one block of code (the power supply registration) earlier, and updates the jump label after a failed registration to point to the correct cleanup. This simple reordering fixes a critical race condition without altering any other logic.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, client->irq, NULL,
                                rt9455_irq_handler_thread,
                                IRQF_TRIGGER_LOW | IRQF_ONESHOT,
                                RT9455_DRIVER_NAME, info);
...
info->charger = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &rt9455_charger_desc,
                                           &rt9455_charger_config);
Reason:
The `devm_` functions free resources in reverse order of allocation. Because `devm_request_threaded_irq` is called before `devm_power_supply_register`, during device removal the power supply is freed first (since it was allocated later). This creates a window where an interrupt can fire after the power supply is freed but before the IRQ handler is unregistered, causing `power_supply_changed()` to access a freed `power_supply` handle. Additionally, during probe an interrupt could fire before the power supply is registered, using an uninitialized handle.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+	info->charger = devm_power_supply_register(dev, &rt9455_charger_desc,
+						   &rt9455_charger_config);
...
 	ret = devm_request_threaded_irq(dev, client->irq, NULL,
 					rt9455_irq_handler_thread,
 					IRQF_TRIGGER_LOW | IRQF_ONESHOT,
 					RT9455_DRIVER_NAME, info);
Reason:
By moving `devm_power_supply_register` before `devm_request_threaded_irq`, the power supply is allocated first. During removal, the IRQ handler is unregistered first (since it was allocated later), so no interrupt can fire after the power supply is freed. This eliminates the use-after-free race and also ensures that the power supply handle is fully initialized before any interrupt can occur during probe.
